posts.headline: Supreme Court Strikes Down Trump Tariffs, Markets Rally
posts.body: The Supreme Court ruled against President Trump's emergency tariffs, sending stocks higher. The S&P 500 gained 0.69% to 6,909.51, while the Nasdaq rose 0.90% to 22,886.07. The Dow added 230.81 points, marking a significant relief rally amid reduced trade uncertainty.

posts.headline: Nasdaq Snaps Five-Week Losing Streak with Tariff Relief
posts.body: The Nasdaq Composite is on track to break its longest weekly losing streak since May 2022, posting a weekly gain of 1.4%. Technology stocks led the rally after the Supreme Court's tariff ruling, with investors shifting focus to earnings and economic data.

posts.headline: CrowdStrike Drops 8% on Anthropic Security Tool Competition
posts.body: CrowdStrike shares fell 8% after Anthropic announced its Claude Code Security tool, capable of finding software bugs and suggesting fixes. The move intensified competition concerns in the cybersecurity sector. Okta dropped 9.2% and Zscaler declined 5.5% on similar fears.

posts.headline: Teradyne Surges on Strong Q4 Earnings 'Blowout'
posts.body: Teradyne (TER) stock surged after reporting fourth-quarter results that 'blew out' analyst expectations. The test equipment maker benefited from strong semiconductor demand. Cognex (CGNX) also posted impressive results, contributing to the industrial sector's momentum.

posts.headline: Walmart Slips 1.5% Despite Strong Quarter
posts.body: Walmart shares declined 1.5% despite reporting strong sales growth in its fourth-quarter earnings. The retail giant's conservative guidance and margin concerns may have outweighed the topline beat. Investors watching for further clarification on full-year outlook.

posts.headline: Carvana Skids 8% on Earnings Miss, Profitability Metrics
posts.body: Carvana stock dropped 8% after the online used car seller missed estimates on key profitability metrics. The company's Q4 results fell short of Wall Street expectations, reigniting concerns about margins in the used vehicle sector. Shares continue to face pressure in a competitive market.
